dedupe_keys.name: spatial database of public health facilities in sub saharan africa maina et al 2019

description: This data set is a geocoded inventory of 98,745 health facilities run by the public health sector in 50 countries and islands of sub-Saharan Africa, assembled from national master facility lists of governments and non-governmental sources and located with several geocoding methods. Each record gives the country, first-level administrative division, facility name, type, ownership and coordinates with the source of the coordinates. The producer is the Population Health Unit of the KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme in Nairobi (Joseph Maina and colleagues), with the World Health Organization's Global Malaria Programme, described in Scientific Data in 2019. Coverage is continental, public-sector facilities only, as compiled in 2018–2019. Files are an Excel workbook and a shapefile, free on figshare and the Humanitarian Data Exchange under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: facility levels follow national definitions that differ between countries, private and faith-based facilities outside the public sector are largely missing, some coordinates are approximate, and the figshare copy is frozen. Simulation uses: facility locations for flood, cyclone and conflict exposure analysis of primary care, accessibility and referral network models, and surge capacity planning in epidemics. Related records: the Malaria Atlas Project travel time maps (data-map-travel-time-to-healthcare) used such lists, and Healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io) is the OpenStreetMap-based alternative.
